[cite:2] h 03deep dive p voice privacy is harder than chat privacy because the same fact exists three times: in the waveform, in the transcript, and in whatever the model copies into a tool argument or a summary. deleting one copy feels like compliance. the other two remain. this room walks the copies. pci ssc’s standards page, fetched 2026-10-14, says pci dss is a baseline for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data or sensitive authentication data, and that qualified security assessors perform assessments. this room does not assign that scope. it does keep a card number out of the model, the log, and the pane. [cite:7] h what counts as sensitive on a call p treat these as sensitive until a written policy says a field is not: payment card numbers, bank numbers, government identifiers, full recordings, authentication secrets, health details a caller volunteers, and the precise location a caller did not need to give. a name plus an account id may be sensitive in combination even when each half looks ordinary. owasp llm02 is the category for putting that material where it does not belong: the prompt, the log, the fine-tune export, the trace vendor. the category does not list your fields for you. you list them, and you mark the list as your policy, not as a finding from a model card. [cite:1] p dtmf digits are not “safer because they were not spoken.” they are often the card number. a media server that logs dtmf for debugging has built a card database. the debug flag is a privacy control. default it off. if you must capture digits to pass them to a payment service, pass them on a channel that service documents, and keep them out of the model context. the model does not need the pan to know that a payment step happened. it needs a result: approved, declined, or failed. the result is not the number. p system prompts are a bad place for secrets and a bad place for a copy of the caller’s data from the previous turn. llm07 says the hidden instruction leaks. anything you put there to “help the model remember the card” will be askable. put the card nowhere near the model. put a token your payment service understands, if the design truly needs a reference, and assume the token can appear in a screenshot.
